claim: Dynamic viscosity of pure water near 293 K is of order one millipascal second, and it changes by roughly two percent per kelvin in that neighbourhood.
validity_conditions: pure water, 288 to 298 K, atmospheric pressure. Not valid for the buffer or glycerol mixtures, and not valid without stating the temperature: the value carries a temperature dependence steep enough to matter in confirm mode. THE NUMBER CITED THIS ENTRY AS ITS OWN SOURCE UNTIL 2026-09-20. It read `kb:water_viscosity_293k`, which left the grade resting on nothing: `kb:<entry_id>` is how a CARD cites the store and INHERITS the entry's grade, and an entry using it points at itself and inherits from itself. The top-level `source` was right the whole time -- `literature:src_water_properties` -- so the fix is the number saying what the entry already said. The grade does not move: `literature` derives E3 either way, which is why check 43 passed it and why it survived. Measured before the fix: one self-citing number in 92 entries, and the only `kb:`-sourced number in the store at all, which is what it should be, since no entry has any business carrying a card's prefix. Check 69 was written for exactly this and held out of the registry until it was clear (a020c32), so no seat's gate reddened over a defect only this one could fix.
